chapter: Recording with King Oliver and Clarence Williams
title: Dave Nelson's arrangements as a check on the sessions
summary: Waters recalls Oliver's cousin Dave Nelson arranging most of the charts, including probably 'Snag It', as another clue for matching sessions.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: He brought in Ben Whitted and he brought in me, see? But he didn't - I don't know what Charlie Irvis, I don't know what Charlie Irvis did any, maybe there. Because I think we had Cuffey, I remember Cuffey real well. Another guy that was there often that you must check on, the cousin of Joe Oliver, and he did the arrangement -
Dave Nelson, he was there, see what I mean? He was there -
Oh, he got there later, so you may be on some of the later ones too.

Yeah, but I mean, I don't know what, I don't know when he got there. But he was there because he was a [ ] in arranging. All the 'rangements that I played, other than the one that I made, only made one - but the, all the arrangements, we played arrangements, you know, we had music, and fake too. But it was Nelson who made that arrangements. See, so that's a good way to check up on that, on those 'rangements. And I think as far as my part was concerned one of those arrangements that you had with "Snag It", made by, I think his name is Dave Nelson, I think.
PS: Dave Nelson, I just said it.
Yeah, Dave Nelson. So if that isn't there, then I'm not there. So that's -
